target_customer: Social media users who want limited-edition face filters and creators who sell filters as collectibles
problem: Face filter creators had no ownership or resale economics on social platforms; Filta used NFTs to give scarcity and creator income.
business_model: Marketplace taking a cut of face filter NFT sales, with in-app purchases
product_category: Face filter NFT marketplace and AR camera app

founders.name: Chris Horne
founders.background_notes: YC page describes the team as veterans of Pixar, Oculus and Facebook and calls him an Emmy and Peabody winner; employer detail from search summaries. Listed under Former Founders on the YC page.

competitors.name: Snapchat Lens Studio
competitors.what: Free AR lens creation tool for creators, with a Creator Marketplace launched in May 2021 for brands to hire creators
competitors.traction_then: Over 2.5 million lenses built by more than 250,000 creators per a later Snap statement; 2021 figures not confirmed

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile AR camera app with face tracking, a marketplace and blockchain ownership is moderate work for a small team of AR veterans.

defensibility.rationale: Filters live on platforms with free tools and the NFT wrapper was easy to copy; no network effect was established.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platforms kept free filter tooling; Meta later shut down Spark AR per a search summary. No sourced outcome for Filta.

market_need_then: NFT trading boomed in 2021 and face filters were popular on Instagram and Snapchat, but creator payment for filters was weak. Demand for owned filters was unproven.

branding.name_origin: Likely shortened from filter, not stated by a source.

identity.voice_and_tone: Founder essays on Notion argue for NFTs and creators, e.g. Why Filta will win

branding.community_and_virality: No press or community found beyond an App Store listing and founder essays.

brand_strength.rationale: No evidence of brand recognition; only an app listing and founder posts.

outcome_analysis: Filta tried to sell limited-edition face filters as NFTs during the 2021 NFT boom, with a Pixar, Oculus and Facebook veteran as founder. The YC page now lists him as a former founder with a team of 3, and no funding or press was found beyond a small YC-era amount in aggregators. The company is still marked active, but the thin trail suggests it stalled; the cause is not public, so these failure factors are inferences about the market rather than stated reasons.
